assumptions: Lower coupling coefficients allow for greater structural divergence.
Variance delta measurements capture structural divergence reliably when noise is controlled.
Previous failures were due to over-dampening rather than lack of divergence.
definition.falsification: If the variance delta remains below 0.0005 even with reduced coupling, the assumption that coupling dampens divergence is likely incorrect, or the system does not exhibit path-dependent divergence under these conditions.
definition.statement: Intelligent systems exhibit detectable path-dependent value divergence when internal coupling parameters are set at lower thresholds (0.85 rather than 0.95) to reduce dampening, resulting in a measurable variance delta of at least 0.0005. Divergence is distinguishable from random noise when the coupling coefficient allows sufficient state freedom.
definition.uncertainty: The relationship between coupling coefficients and variance delta is likely non-linear; the new threshold is an estimate.
